answer: Marble Canyon Garden: one fake costs a $4-a-month VPS in its own data center. The verifier drops a marble — one probe packet — down the canyon of network distance to that server, timing the fall from three public RIPE Atlas probes. The garden is the public table of those depths: a farm claiming servers in ten cities from a single rack shows depths that don't match the map, and the garden pulls the whole cluster out by its roots. A server that moves cities starts over with a fresh 30-day bed of readings.
